account: Veterinarians at Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich ran a blinded prospective study on a conventional one-site piglet-producing farm in Germany. Its nursery holds 600 pigs per airspace in 20 pens. Two batches were monitored for 39 days each. Two SoundTalks monitors (SoundTalks NV, Leuven) counted coughs around the clock and distinguished pig coughs from other barn noise. They computed a daily respiratory health status from 0 to 100, with yellow alerts at 40–59 and red at 0–39. The LEDs were set to a blinded “science mode” so that the investigators were not cued. Oral fluids and bioaerosol samples were screened by qPCR for swine influenza A virus, PRRSV, Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae, Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae and PCV2. All but M. hyopneumoniae were detected. High loads of swine influenza A virus RNA were significantly associated with a decrease in the AI-calculated respiratory health score. Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica funded the study, and three of its employees are co-authors. The paper was published on 6 October 2024. In a separate study published on 20 December 2024, researchers at Sunchon National University with no external funding kept 80 pigs in two houses under normal or poor conditions of heat, humidity and gases. The SoundTalks respiratory score averaged 97.55 under normal conditions and 74.41 under poor conditions. In 2026, a trial at Konkuk University in Korea used the same device's respiratory health status as an outcome measure across 2,000 grower-finisher pigs.

ai_role.statement: The AI produced a respiratory health score that tracked swine influenza A loads measured by qPCR. Alerts were hidden from investigators, so the study measures association rather than any alert that changed what happened. Funding and three co-authors came from Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica. The paper states the funders were not involved in collection, analysis or interpretation.

Oral fluids and bioaerosol samples were screened by qPCR for swine influenza A virus, PRRSV, Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae, Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae and PCV2. All but M. hyopneumoniae were detected. High loads of swine influenza A virus RNA were significantly associated with a decrease in the AI-calculated respiratory health score. Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica funded the study, and three of its employees are co-authors. The paper was published on 6 October 2024. In a separate study published on 20 December 2024, researchers at Sunchon National University with no external funding kept 80 pigs in two houses under normal or poor conditions of heat, humidity and gases. The SoundTalks respiratory score averaged 97.55 under normal conditions and 74.41 under poor conditions. In 2026, a trial at Konkuk University in Korea used the same device's respiratory health status as an outcome measure across 2,000 grower-finisher pigs.
